q: 1. Which of the following error is not eliminated by the method of repetition of horizontal angle measurement?
options: Error due to eccentricity of verniers
Error due to displacement of station signals
Error due to wrong adjustment of line of collimation and trunnion axis
explain: If the station signal itself has moved or is displaced, repeating the angle measurement from the same (wrong) signal location will not fix the error.

q: 2. The distance between terminal points computed from a subsidiary traverse run between them, is generally known as
explain: When a subsidiary (auxiliary) traverse is run between two points to establish the distance between them, the computed distance is called the traverse base.

q: 3. The included angles of a theodolite traverse, are generally measured
explain: Included angles in a theodolite traverse are conventionally measured clockwise, starting the observation from the back (previous) station and swinging to the forward station.

q: 4. The latitude of a traverse leg is obtained by multiplying its length by
explain: Latitude (the north-south component) of a traverse leg = Length x cosine(reduced bearing), since latitude is the projection of the line onto the north-south axis.

q: 5. In a closed traverse, sum of south latitudes exceeds the sum of north latitudes and the sum of east departures exceeds the sum of west departures, then, the closing line will lie in
explain: The closing error (line needed to close the traverse) runs opposite to the net imbalance; since the traverse itself trends south and east, the closing line to bring it back runs north and west, i.e. lies in the north-west quadrant.

q: 6. An axis about which the telescope can be rotated in a horizontal plane is called
explain: Rotation in a horizontal plane happens around the vertical axis. Rotation in a vertical plane happens around the horizontal (trunnion) axis.

q: 7. Axis of altitude level is
options: parallel to the line of collimation
explain: The altitude level (attached to the telescope) has its axis parallel to the line of collimation of the telescope, so it can be used to check/set the line of sight horizontal even when the telescope's own bubble is out of adjustment.

q: 8. In precision theodolite traverse... the angular error of closure should not exceed
explain: For standard/ordinary traversing, the error is often capped at $1' \sqrt{N}$, where N is the number of stations.

q: 9. The most commonly used set of theodolite operations are
explain: The standard convention for taking a 'set' of theodolite observations is to start with the face-left position swinging right (clockwise), then observe face-right swinging left.

q: 10. When the first object is to be focused, the scale, is set to 0 deg 00'00" and then
options: the upper screw is fixed , lower screw released, the object sighted, lower screw fixed and lower tangent screw operated
both the clamp screw fixed, to tangent screw operated
bottom clamp screw fixed, top screw released, the object sighted and upper tangent screw operated
object is exactly bisected by operating both the upper and lower tangent screws whichever is convenient.
explain: The standard procedure to set an initial zero reading is: fix the upper clamp, release the lower clamp, roughly sight the object, then fix the lower clamp and use the lower tangent screw to bisect the object exactly.

q: 11. Traversing is generally done by
explain: A traverse survey can be carried out using a chain (chain traversing), a compass, a theodolite, or a plane table, depending on the accuracy required, so all methods are applicable.

q: 12. If 'n' is the number of sides, then the total sum of exterior angles of a closed traverse should be
explain: Since interior and exterior angles at each vertex are supplementary and their total for all n vertices is 4 right angles more than the interior sum, the sum of exterior angles works out to (2n + 4) x 90 degrees.

q: 13. An angle measured clockwise from the proceeding survey line to the following survey line is called
explain: A deflection angle is measured from the prolongation of the preceding line to the following line, and when the direction is clockwise, it is a right deflection angle.

q: 14. For which of the following permanent adjustments of theodolite, the spire test is used?
explain: The spire test is specifically used to check and adjust the horizontal (trunnion) axis of a theodolite, ensuring it is truly horizontal by sighting a high point from both faces.

q: 15. An angle between the inclined line of sight and the horizontal is called .............
explain: A vertical angle is the angle measured in the vertical plane between the line of sight and the horizontal line.

q: 16. The angle between the prolongation of the preceding line and the forward line of a traverse is called
explain: As defined earlier (Q210), this angle between the prolongation of the preceding survey line and the following line is the deflection angle.

q: 17. Right face and left reading are taken to .............
options: eliminate error of trunnion axis not exactly horizontal
eliminate error in the line of collimation
explain: Changing the face of the theodolite (Face Left and Face Right) eliminates errors due to the line of collimation not being perpendicular to the trunnion axis and the trunnion axis not being perpendicular to the vertical axis.

q: 18. After levelling of an instrument is done what is the next up?
explain: After the temporary adjustment of levelling the instrument is complete, the next step is to release all the clamping screws so that the instrument is free for sighting.

q: 19. Theodolite is an instrument used for measuring
explain: Theodolites are versatile instruments designed for precise angular measurements in both planes.

q: 20. A traverse deflection angle is .............
options: the difference between the included angle and 180°
the difference between 360° and the included angle
explain: A deflection angle is the angle which a survey line makes with the prolongation of the preceding line. It is calculated by subtracting the included angle from 180°.

q: 21. When the whole circle bearing of a traverse line is between 90° and 180° then .............
options: the latitude is positive and departure is negative
the departure is positive and latitude is negative
both the latitude and departure are positive
both the latitude and departure are negative
explain: The range 90° to 180° falls in the second quadrant (S-E). In this quadrant, Latitude (L cos θ) is South (negative) and Departure (L sin θ) is East (positive).

q: 22. A 20 cm theodolite means
options: diameter of the lower plate is 20 cm
diameter of the upper plate is 20 cm
total height of theodolite plate is 20 cm
explain: As per standard nomenclature, the measurement refers to the diameter of the lower graduated horizontal plate.

q: 23. The projection of a line on a plane perpendicular to meridian is known as
explain: Departure is the orthographic projection of a line onto the East-West axis (L sin θ), which is perpendicular to the meridian.

q: 24. When the angular and linear measurements are equally precise in traversing, the balancing of a traverse is done by .............
explain: Bowditch's rule (Compass Rule) is used when linear and angular measurements are of equal precision. It assumes errors in linear measurements are proportional to √L.

q: 25. The outer spindle attached to the lower plate in a transit theodolite known is
explain: The lower plate carries the main graduated scale and is attached to the outer spindle; hence it is called the scale plate.

q: 26. An angle made by a survey line with the prolongation of the proceeding line, is known as .............
explain: A deflection angle is the angle between the preceding line's extension and the next line in the traverse.

q: 27. The telescope is said to be normal when the
options: bubble of the telescope is down and the face of the vertical circle is right
bubble of the telescope is up and the face of the vertical circle is left
bubble of the telescope is up and the face of the vertical circle is right
explain: Telescope Normal (or Face Left) is the standard position where the vertical circle is to the left of the observer and the bubble is on top.

q: 28. The process of bringing the vertical circle to the right of the observer is called
explain: Changing face is the operation of transiting the telescope and swinging it 180 degrees to switch from Face Left to Face Right (or vice versa).

q: 29. The error eliminated by taking mean of both face observations is
options: error due to eccentricity of verniers
error due to imperfect adjustment of levels
error due to line of collimation not being perpendicular to horizontal axis
explain: Taking the mean of Face Left and Face Right cancels out errors caused by the line of collimation not being perfectly perpendicular to the horizontal axis.

q: 30. The difference between the sum of the measured angles and the theoretical sum of the angles of a closed traverse is called the
explain: The error found by comparing the sum of observed angles with (2N ± 4) × 90° is the angular closing error.

q: 31. The difference between the two bearings of the last line as observed at the first and the last station of a traverse is known as
explain: If the computed bearing of the final line doesn't match its measured bearing, the difference is the closing error in bearing.

q: 32. A plumb bob is required .............
options: when measuring distances along slopes in a hilly country
for accurate centering of a theodolite over a station mark
for testing the vertically of ranging poles
explain: A plumb bob is an essential tool for transferring points vertically, centering instruments, and ensuring verticality.

q: 33. A traverse consists of six side, then the sum of external angle must be
explain: The sum of exterior angles is (2N + 4) × 90°. For N=6, (12 + 4) × 90 = 16 × 90 = 1440°.

q: 34. The distance between terminal points computed from a subsidiary traverse run between them is known as
explain: A traverse base refers to the line connecting the start and end points of a traverse segment.

q: 35. Axis method of traverse correction is used when
options: the angles are measured very accurately
the lengths are measured very accurately
both (a) and (b) are not measured very accurately
explain: The Axis method is specialized for cases where angular precision far exceeds linear precision.

q: 36. Right face and left face reading are taken to
options: eliminate error of trunnion axis not exactly horizontal
eliminate error in the line of collimation
explain: While it also helps with collimation (Q319), the provided answer specifically highlights the trunnion (horizontal) axis error.

q: 37. To avoid large centering error with very short legs, observations are generally made
options: to a target fixed on theodolite tripod
explain: When traverse legs are short, even a small displacement in centering causes a large angular error. Using high-precision optical plummet systems and fixed targets minimizes this risk.

q: 38. You have to observe an included angle with better accuracy than what is achievable by a vernier, you will prefer the method of .............
explain: The method of repetition allows the same angle to be measured multiple times and divided by the number of repetitions, which reduces the least-count error.

q: 39. In horizontal angles, the error due to imperfect leveling of the plate bubble is .............
options: large when sights are nearly level
explain: If the instrument is not level, the horizontal axis is not horizontal; this error is magnified significantly when the telescope is tilted steeply upward or downward.

q: 40. An angle between the inclined line of sight and the horizontal is called .............
explain: Vertical angles are measured in the vertical plane between the horizontal line of sight and the target line.

q: 41. Can the vertical axis coincide with any other axis in any position of telescope?
options: Yes, with the geometric centre of level head
Yes, with the axis of altitude levels
explain: In specific adjustment positions, the vertical axis can align with the axis of the altitude bubble tube to ensure horizontal rotation.

q: 42. For a transit theodolite the least reading on the main scale is 20'. If its vernier scale should read 20", then .............
options: 59° on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
20° on the main scale are divided into 60 equal divisions
19° 40' on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
20° 20' on the main scale are divided into 60 equal parts
explain: For a least count of 20", the vernier must divide $(n-1)$ divisions of the main scale. Here, 59 divisions of 20' each ($19° 40'$) are divided into 60 parts on the vernier.
